name: Thompson Sampling and Deep RL Hybrid (Beta-Posterior-Gated Actor-Critic)
key_paper: Russo, D., Van Roy, B., Kazerouni, A., Osband, I., Wen, Z. (2018). A Tutorial on Thompson Sampling. Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning, 11(1), 1-96. Hybrid framing informed by Osband et al. (2016) Deep Exploration via Bootstrapped DQN, NeurIPS 2016, and by Dann et al. (2021) Adapting to Misspecification in Contextual Bandits, NeurIPS 2021.
algorithm_description: The hybrid combines a Beta-posterior Thompson Sampling bandit (one per lottery) with a deep Actor-Critic policy gradient loop. After each scored draw the Beta(alpha, beta) posterior for that lottery is updated: alpha += hits, beta += misses. A fresh Thompson weight w ~ Beta(alpha, beta) is then drawn and used as a multiplicative gate on the Actor-Critic policy gradient update for that lottery: the gradient step is scaled by w before being applied, so lotteries with higher empirical hit rates receive larger gradient updates and effectively drive more of the shared encoder's learning signal. Lotteries with low weight (low confidence) revert to higher exploration temperature via temperature_from_weight(), diversifying generated plays rather than reinforcing a weak policy. This creates a closed feedback loop: draw -> score -> Thompson update -> gated gradient -> updated Actor -> new plays.
action_space_handling: The Actor is the existing SharedLotteryTransformer encoder plus a per-lottery softmax head producing a probability distribution over the ball pool (size 50, 49, or 49 depending on lottery). The Thompson weight gates how aggressively the Actor is updated, not how the action space is represented. Action sampling remains autoregressive with masking to enforce the combinatorial constraint. The bandit weight acts as a meta-controller on top of the existing discrete action space.
how_combinatorial_output_is_formed: Autoregressive masking over the per-lottery softmax head: the Actor selects one number at a time, masks it to -inf logit, then selects the next until k numbers are chosen. The temperature fed to the softmax is derived from the Thompson weight via temperature_from_weight(w, t_min=0.8, t_max=1.6) -- already implemented in bandit.py -- so the combinatorial sampling diversity is directly modulated by the Beta posterior confidence. High-confidence lotteries generate more concentrated (lower-temperature) plays; low-confidence lotteries generate more exploratory plays.
sequential_generation_strategy: Autoregressive: numbers are generated one at a time from the per-lottery softmax head, with previously selected numbers masked out. Each selection step is conditioned on the state embedding from the shared transformer encoder plus the already-selected set (encoded as a running multi-hot mask appended to the decoder input). This allows inter-number correlations to be modeled through the shared encoder context, though the benefit is limited given very short draw histories.
gradient_estimator_type: REINFORCE (score function / likelihood-ratio estimator) is the natural choice for the policy gradient component given the discrete combinatorial action space. The Thompson weight w acts as a per-lottery scalar multiplier on the REINFORCE gradient: grad_theta_lottery = w * sum_t [R - b] * grad log pi(a_t | s_t), where b is a baseline (e.g., exponential moving average of recent rewards). This reduces gradient variance for high-confidence lotteries (large w amplifies signal) and dampens potentially harmful gradient steps for low-confidence lotteries (small w suppresses noisy updates). The REINFORCE estimator is unbiased but high-variance; the Thompson gating does not reduce estimator variance directly but does reduce the magnitude of destructive updates on small datasets.
combinatorial_constraint_enforcement: Autoregressive masking: after selecting number i, its logit is set to -inf before the next softmax, guaranteeing all k selected numbers are distinct. Exactly k steps are run, enforcing the cardinality constraint. The Thompson weight does not affect constraint enforcement -- it is applied only to the gradient update magnitude, not to the sampling procedure itself.
sample_efficiency_rating: Medium. The Beta posterior accumulates evidence across all scored draws for a given lottery (~100 draws per lottery currently), making the Thompson weight a low-variance summary of historical accuracy. This is more sample-efficient than learning a separate meta-policy from scratch. However, the underlying Actor-Critic policy gradient still requires many reward signals to learn useful number preferences, and with n<200 draws the REINFORCE gradient variance remains high. The gating mechanism prevents catastrophic forgetting (low-weight lotteries are not over-updated) but does not itself provide the signal needed to learn number-level preferences. Rated medium rather than high because the gating is a stabilizer, not a data amplifier.
regularization_built_in: Three built-in regularization mechanisms: (1) Thompson gating -- the Beta(alpha, beta) weight naturally shrinks toward 0.5 (the uninformative prior mean) when a lottery has few scored draws, preventing over-confident gradient steps early in training. (2) Temperature inflation -- low-weight lotteries automatically receive higher sampling temperature (up to t_max=1.6 in bandit.py), acting as entropy regularization on the Actor. (3) Beta prior -- starting from Beta(1,1) = Uniform[0,1], the prior encodes no preference before any draws are scored, preventing the bandit from locking onto early noise. The Actor-Critic itself can additionally use entropy bonus and weight decay as standard policy gradient regularizers.
known_failure_modes_on_small_data: Weight starvation: if one lottery consistently scores 0 hits (lottery-level bad luck, not model failure), its beta parameter grows rapidly while alpha stagnates, driving w toward 0 and suppressing all gradient updates for that lottery. This creates a positive-feedback loop where the lottery never improves because it is never trained. Fix: impose a minimum gradient gate (e.g., w_min = 0.1) to ensure all lotteries receive some training signal. Posterior conflation: the Beta posterior aggregates hits across all draws equally, conflating old and recent performance -- a model that improved recently but performed poorly historically will be underweighted. Fix: exponential decay on alpha/beta increments (align with the existing recency_weights() decay=0.92 in feedback.py). Gating instability: if the Actor-Critic loss landscape is non-convex (common with transformer fine-tuning), scaling gradients by a stochastic Beta sample introduces additional gradient noise on top of REINFORCE variance, potentially destabilizing training early on.
data_regime_evidence: No published paper directly benchmarks a Thompson-gated policy gradient system on fewer than 200 training samples in a combinatorial prediction task. Thompson Sampling itself has finite-sample regret bounds (Russo et al. 2018, Theorem 3: O(sqrt(KT log K)) Bayesian regret after T rounds for K arms), but these bounds apply to the bandit layer, not to the Actor-Critic underneath. The lottery-nn project provides its own validation regime: ~100 draws per lottery, scored via score_log.csv, which is sufficient to observe whether the Thompson weight correlates with hit rate improvement over time. minimum_training_samples_tested: [uncertain] (no external benchmark). performance_degradation_curve: [uncertain]. comparison_baseline: [uncertain] -- internal comparison against unweighted Actor-Critic updates is the recommended ablation.
convergence_guarantees_small_n: The Beta posterior converges to the true hit rate in expectation as draws accumulate (Beta-Binomial conjugate model is well understood). However, convergence of the underlying Actor-Critic policy under Thompson-gated REINFORCE with n<200 has no published finite-sample guarantee. The gating mechanism inherits the asymptotic convergence properties of REINFORCE (converges to a local optimum under standard Robbins-Monro conditions) but slows convergence for low-confidence lotteries by design. In practice, convergence speed on n<200 is [uncertain] and likely lottery-specific depending on the true signal-to-noise ratio of the historical data.
reward_distribution_handling: The Thompson weight is computed from cumulative hits and misses, which already aggregates the sparse, skewed reward distribution (~95% zero-hit, ~4% 1-2 hits, rare 3+). Because alpha and beta accumulate across all draws, individual zero-reward draws contribute beta+=main_count without destabilizing the posterior -- the Beta distribution is robust to long runs of zeros. The Actor-Critic reward signal beneath the gating still suffers from sparsity; the Thompson gate does not reshape the reward distribution, it only modulates how much the policy updates in response to it. Distributional return modeling (e.g., QR-DQN) is not built in but can be added to the Critic alongside the Thompson gate. Minimum draws for meaningful Thompson weight: approximately 20-30 scored draws before alpha/beta differ significantly from the Beta(1,1) prior.
credit_assignment_granularity: The Beta posterior in bandit.py uses play-level credit: hits = main-ball hits on the best-scoring line. The Actor-Critic underneath can operate at number-level credit if REINFORCE is applied per autoregressive step (semi-bandit feedback: reward step t = 1 if number selected at step t appears in the draw, 0 otherwise). Combining number-level REINFORCE reward with lottery-level Thompson gating is a natural hybrid: fine-grained learning signal per number, coarse-grained confidence gate per lottery. This combination is more informative than either mechanism alone and is particularly valuable at n<200 where play-level credit is very sparse.
diversity_mechanism: Two diversity mechanisms operate jointly: (1) Thompson temperature inflation -- low-weight lotteries sample from a higher-temperature softmax (up to t_max=1.6), producing more diverse number selections across plays. (2) REINFORCE entropy bonus -- an optional entropy term H(pi) added to the policy gradient loss encourages the Actor to maintain a broad distribution, preventing mode collapse to a small set of frequently selected numbers. These two mechanisms complement each other: the Thompson gate controls inter-lottery diversity (which lottery's Actor is updated more), while the entropy bonus controls intra-lottery diversity (how varied the generated plays are within one lottery).
offline_vs_online_rl_compatibility: Highly compatible with offline training. The Beta posterior is updated from the existing score_log.csv (historical hit scores) without requiring new environment interaction. The Actor-Critic component can be trained offline using the full historical draw dataset (draws.csv, draws_649.csv, draws_dailygrand.csv) as a fixed replay, with each draw treated as an offline trajectory: state = encoded draw history, action = generated play from last predict run, reward = scored hits. New environment interaction occurs only once per week when a real draw is logged via main_swarm.py log, at which point both the Beta posterior and the Actor-Critic are updated. This matches the operational cadence perfectly.
complexity: Medium. The Thompson bandit (bandit.py) is already implemented. The new work is: (1) a lightweight Actor head on top of the SharedLotteryTransformer encoder, (2) a REINFORCE training loop with Thompson weight gating, (3) wiring the scored hits from score_log.csv into both the bandit update and the Actor gradient. No new major libraries are required.
key_dependencies: PyTorch (already installed). numpy (already used in bandit.py). No external RL library required -- the Thompson gating and REINFORCE loop are self-contained. Optional: torchrl for replay buffer utilities.
estimated_lines_of_code: 200-300 lines: Actor head with autoregressive masking (~60 lines), REINFORCE loss function with Thompson weight gate (~40 lines), offline training loop over historical draws (~70 lines), wiring bandit.update() into the training loop (~20 lines), prediction wrapper using temperature_from_weight() already in bandit.py (~30 lines), integration with main_swarm.py log/predict commands (~50 lines).
transfer_learning_compatibility: Excellent. The SharedLotteryTransformer encoder is already trained and produces lottery-conditioned state embeddings. The Thompson-gated Actor-Critic attaches a small MLP Actor head to the frozen encoder output -- no retraining from scratch. The lottery_id embedding already differentiates lotteries, so the same encoder serves all three bandit arms. The existing temperature_from_weight() function in bandit.py is already the correct interface point between the Beta posterior and the Actor's sampling temperature. The integration is additive: nothing in the existing codebase needs to be replaced, only extended.
specific_application_in_project: This is the primary Phase 2 implementation target. The Thompson bandit (bandit.py) is already complete and tracking per-lottery hit rates. Phase 2 adds the Actor-Critic on top: (1) A per-lottery Actor MLP head is attached to the SharedLotteryTransformer encoder output in model_swarm.py. (2) After each draw is logged via main_swarm.py log --lottery X, bandit.update() is called (already implemented) to update the Beta posterior for lottery X, yielding a new Thompson weight w. (3) The offline REINFORCE loop then runs N gradient steps on that lottery's Actor, with each gradient step scaled by w. Low-confidence lotteries (e.g., Daily Grand with few scored draws) receive damped updates; high-confidence lotteries drive the shared encoder's adaptation. (4) At prediction time, temperature_from_weight(w) already maps the Beta sample to a sampling temperature for the autoregressive Actor. (5) Score tracking in score_log.csv feeds directly into bandit.update() after each real draw. This replaces the current static temperature-softmax sampling in predict.py with a fully adaptive, confidence-gated policy that tightens or loosens based on empirical draw-by-draw feedback.
replaces_or_extends: Extends: the Beta posterior in bandit.py is already in place and is not replaced. The Actor-Critic is added as a new training loop on top of the existing SharedLotteryTransformer encoder. The Thompson weight gate is a new wiring between the existing bandit.update() output and the new REINFORCE gradient step. Replaces temperature-softmax sampling in src/predict.py with Thompson-temperature autoregressive Actor sampling.
existing_open_source_implementations: No published library implements Thompson-gated REINFORCE as a first-class abstraction. The components exist separately: (1) Thompson Sampling: numpy.random.beta() -- already used in bandit.py. (2) REINFORCE: standard PyTorch implementation, widely available (e.g., OpenAI Spinning Up reinforce.py, CleanRL). (3) The gating combination is a project-specific design. Reference implementations to study: Osband et al. Bootstrapped DQN (github.com/deepmind/bsuite) for posterior-driven exploration in deep RL; Riquelme et al. Deep Bayesian Bandits Showdown (ICLR 2018) for Thompson Sampling applied to neural contextual bandits. The lottery-nn bandit.py is itself a complete reference for the Thompson layer.
benchmark_results: Thompson Sampling alone: Chapelle & Li (2011, WWW) demonstrated Thompson Sampling outperforms UCB1 and epsilon-greedy on click-through-rate prediction tasks with sparse binary reward -- structurally similar to lottery hit/miss feedback. Russo et al. (2018) prove O(sqrt(KT log K)) Bayesian regret bounds for K-armed Thompson Sampling. Thompson-gated policy gradient hybrids: no direct published benchmark exists. The closest analogs are Bayesian actor-critic methods (e.g., BDQN, Bayesian Policy Gradient) which show improved sample efficiency over vanilla policy gradient in sparse-reward settings but are evaluated on standard RL benchmarks (MuJoCo, Atari), not combinatorial prediction tasks with n<200 draws.
notable_use_cases: 1. Online recommendation systems: Thompson Sampling over item arms to gate which recommendation policy receives gradient updates -- structurally identical to gating per-lottery Actor-Critic updates. 2. Clinical trial adaptive allocation (Berry et al. 2010): Thompson Sampling assigns more patients to better-performing treatment arms while continuing to update all arms -- analogous to concentrating training signal on lotteries with higher hit rates while maintaining exploration for others. 3. Multi-task RL with task-level bandit (e.g., Graves et al. 2017, NeurIPS, Automated Curriculum Learning): a bandit selects which task to train on next based on learning progress -- directly analogous to using Thompson weight to gate gradient updates across the three lotteries sharing one encoder backbone. 4. Contextual bandit for news article recommendation (Agrawal & Goyal 2013, ICML): Thompson Sampling with neural features, showing robustness to reward sparsity -- matching the lottery domain's ~95% zero-reward draws.
